securityAcceptance: Source/build-surface review for #1649 adds HEVC/HDR normalization, explicitly pinned OpenH264 encoder and zimg color conversion. The existing optional role remains bounded/default-off outside authorized operator rollout. Source hardening regressions execute in every restricted build.

CVE-2025-52290.review: Upstream range remains undetermined. The published reporter describes an AAC allocation misinterpreted by the H.264 helper after a failed codec switch. The pinned helper only guarded null private data/SPS; guard-h264-context.patch now checks the actual allocated decoder and requested codec before reading private state. The build executes test-h264-context.c with an AAC decoder, H.264 codec ID and inaccessible private pointer, plus null and uninitialized H.264 cases. MPEG-TS is also absent and input is forced MOV. This is a reviewed local defense for the shipped surface, not a claim that upstream marks the CVE resolved.

CVE-2026-107675.review: Affected protocol, demuxer or decoder is not compiled in the restricted build. Input format forced MOV; only the explicitly reviewed H.264/HEVC and AAC/MP3/PCM audio decoding surface and file/pipe protocols are enabled. See original advisory description and build configuration.

CVE-2026-107676.review: HEVC decoding makes this applicable. initialize-hdr-payload.patch initializes every serialized HDR10+ byte and writes color-saturation flags outside the optional tone-mapping branch, matching the parser and size calculation. Every build executes test-hdr-payload.c with one/three windows, no tone mapping, saturation flags, oppositely poisoned caller buffers, round-trip parsing and guard bytes. Only selected media are normalized; frame side data and H.264 SEI are removed and output is revalidated. Matroska/AV1 stay absent. This is a reviewed local defense, not an upstream closure claim.

openh264.review: Pinned upstream 2.7.0 encoder; Debian records no unresolved sid finding. Earlier decoding issues, including CVE-2025-27091, are fixed by this version. FFmpeg does not enable the OpenH264 decoder. Native untrusted decoding stays in its explicitly enabled FFmpeg decoders. Cisco binary-license/patent coverage is not claimed for source builds.

zimg.review: Pinned upstream source, static color-conversion filters. Debian currently records no zimg advisories; absence from that feed is not vulnerability-free certification. No new input format/network parser or remote content flow.

CVE-2026-6385.review: The current primary Debian JSON marks sid resolved, so this finding is no longer in the unresolved-feed set checked by check-advisories.py. The updated description concerns DVD subtitle fragment reassembly reached by MPEG-PS/VOB input. The pinned restricted build still starts with --disable-everything and enables only the MOV demuxer and explicit H.264/HEVC/audio parsers and decoders, excluding MPEG-PS/VOB and DVD subtitle parsing/decoding; runtime input is forced MOV. This does not claim the pinned upstream commit contains a fix or that arbitrary system FFmpeg is safe. An unresolved reappearance remains a new guard failure. Existing restricted binary/runtime gates remain mandatory.
